title: C# Questions & Answers - Fundamentals of Exception Handling
sourceFile: Exception Handling Fundamentals - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on fundamentals of the exception handling in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT an exception in C#?
questions.explanation: Exceptions are runtime errors. An incorrect arithmetic expression is a syntax error that is caught by the compiler at compile-time, not an exception thrown during execution.

questions.question: Which of the following is the base class for all exceptions in the .NET Framework?
questions.explanation: In C#, all exception types must derive from the 'System.Exception' base class. 'StackUnderflowException' does not exist in the standard .NET library.

questions.question: What is the object-oriented way to handle runtime errors in C#?
questions.explanation: Exceptions provide a structured, object-oriented approach to error handling, separating error-detection code from error-handling code.

questions.question: Which statement describes an advantage of exception handling over traditional error-handling methods?

options.text: Exceptions cannot be accidentally ignored like error codes can
It separates the main logic from error-handling logic
The try-catch-finally structure ensures cleanup code always runs

questions.explanation: Exception handling makes code cleaner, more robust, and more maintainable by providing a dedicated mechanism for dealing with unexpected runtime situations.

questions.question: When does an Exception occur in a C# application?
questions.explanation: An exception is an error that happens during the execution of a program (runtime). Errors during compilation are called syntax errors.

questions.question: Which of these keywords is NOT a part of the C# exception handling mechanism?
questions.explanation: C# uses four keywords for exception handling: try, catch, finally, and throw. 'thrown' and 'throws' (Java) are not used in C#.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to wrap a block of code that might throw an exception so it can be monitored?
questions.explanation: The 'try' block encloses the guarded code. If an exception occurs within this block, the runtime looks for a matching catch handler.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to manually signal the occurrence of an exception?
questions.explanation: The 'throw' keyword is used to raise an exception manually, either by re-throwing a caught exception or creating a new exception object.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The array has a size of 4 (indices 0-3). Accessing index 5 triggers an IndexOutOfRangeException, which is caught. The program then continues to the next line.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Division by zero throws a DivideByZeroException. Since DivideByZeroException inherits from ArithmeticException, the catch block is executed and prints 'Java'.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about 'finally' is WRONG?

options.text: The finally clause is used for cleanup operations
A single try block can have multiple finally clauses
Finally executes whether or not an exception was thrown
Finally is optional in a try-catch structure

questions.explanation: In C#, a 'try' block can be followed by multiple 'catch' blocks, but only ONE 'finally' block is allowed.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: Program prints 'Java' and then crashes with a DivideByZeroException

questions.explanation: The division by zero throws an exception. Before the program crashes or propagates the error, the 'finally' block is guaranteed to execute, printing 'Java'.
